Playtime

For scale: 45 stages at a 20:00 countdown is 15 hours of clock alone, before boss fights past 0:00, menus and build choices. There is no measured full-clear time in the data.

Status key

  • Playable: reachable from the stage select in a normal build. All 15 acts are playable.
  • Planned or deferred: not in the game; listed only at the end, in their own section.
Campaign: acts and stages

The 15 acts in three Parts

ActPartNameStatusStagesShared rulesReckoning at 0:00
IPart IThe Crimson CovenantPlayableGraveyard, Crimson March, SanctumNo shared act rules (the baseline). Stage mechanics: Graveyard empowered graves, desecration and Crypt Defender; Crimson March battle zones, outposts, ward generators, supply carts; Sanctum ward chambers, sacred altars, floor corruption.The Reckoning / Dawn's Wrath
IIPart IThe Black TidePlayableCutter, Galleon, MaelstromBoarding (boats pull alongside and pour crews aboard; the one spawn route), the Deck (the ship is the arena; a foe knocked past the rail drowns), Strikes from the Sea (swimmers surface on telegraphed circles that hit both armies).The Black Tide (the whole rail boards at once, the rail is struck every 3 s, a great wave every 20 s)
IIIPart IThe Sanguine CourtPlayableRavensmoor, The Witchwood, Castle SanguisBloodfeast (enemies heal on hits, blood shield), Night Wings (bats fly over the ring), the Blood Moon every 4:00 for 45 s.The Endless Feast (Blood Moon never sets, coffins release Vampire Nobles)
IVPart IThe Last LinePlayableSkid Row, Fort Kessler, Liberty HeightsCity blocks arenas, a clock escalation (gangs, police, SWAT, army, heroes), Armour (frontal cuts, vehicles, wrecks), Supers, Civilians.Martial Law (every tier at once, artillery lines, the Supers return)
VPart IThe Shogunate of the Rising SunPlayableThe Province, Kurogane, The Sun RoadThe Sun's Course (day, dusk, night with darkness and lit lanterns), the Draw (iai cuts), From the Shadows (ambushes revealed by light).The Endless Night
VIPart IIThe Hall of the SlainPlayableBarrow Fields, Valgard, VigridThe Long Winter (the cold closes in; braziers are warmth, doused by frost giants and seers, relit by the necromancer), Berserkergang, Rune-Stones.Ragnarok (eight Einherjar march at once, fire-giants every 30 s, every valkyrie dives)
VIIPart IIThe Necropolis DynastyPlayableNecropolis, Lioness Temple, Two TruthsRebirth and the Names (fallen Dynasty bodies return unless their Canopic Jar is broken; cartouche timers), the Black Land and the Sandstorm, Heka (glyphs that jump between summons).The Devourer's Hour (Rebirth has no limit, the Sandstorm never ends, the Devourer's shadow runs along telegraphed lanes)
VIIIPart IIThe Olympian RepublicPlayableIlion, Olympus, UnderworldWrath of the Gods (waves, lightning, fissures hitting both armies), Phalanx (shield fronts), Glory (Heroes grow with kills).The Twilight of the Gods (Bronze Titans)
IXPart IIThe InfernoPlayableThe Gate, The Palace, PandemoniumHell Pits, Portals (sealable), Temptation (succubi charm summons).The Last Judgment (portals open, pits open faster, the Adversary's hand)
XPart IIThe Celestial HostPlayableSilver Stair, Wheel of Thrones, EmpyreanJudgment (the scales of the necromancer's sins), Hallowed Light (shafts only shade and barriers stop), Grace (each halo ignores the first hit of each damage type); low cloud banks give shade.The Last Trumpet (seven trumpets: each fills the scales, widens the Light and rings the necromancer with Virtues; then the sky opens)
XIPart IIIThe Ancient EyePlayableGullhaven, Archive, Ul-ThalosDread (damage taken +5% per 25), Claims (fallen summons rise as hostile Drowned Thralls). Tide, ink wells, sinking island on the stages.The Deep Rises / The Stacks Unwrite Themselves / The Waking
XIIPart IIIThe Electronic EmpirePlayableScrap Wastes, Assembly Halls, Iron CitadelLine of Fire, Lock-On, Steel has no soul (machines leave no corpse; cyborgs rise as Grave Gunners).Purge Protocol (kill-drones, orbital strikes)
XIIIPart IIIThe Concord of StarsPlayableCrash Site, Proving Moon, The ArkBeams (only Bone Walls stop them, barriers reflect them), Abduction (saucers lift summons away), Terraforming (alien turf heals Concord units; spells burn it back). Crash Site: Infestation eggs. Proving Moon: low gravity. Ark: vault beasts, reactor vents, reaping emitters.The Final Harvest (the mothership's eye opens, saucers fill the sky, the abduction cap is gone)
XIVPart IIIThe Age of TitansPlayableFern Basin, Great Plain, Last DayPacks (a pack leader and its alpha), Herds (stampedes that run away from what hurt the herd), Scavengers; every obstacle shelters from a stampede. Fern Basin tar seeps, Great Plain watering hole and canyon, Last Day meteorites.The Stampede of Ash (Fern Basin, Great Plain: herds from every side, volcanic bombs); the Extinction (Last Day: a white-out, every enemy dies, the dead rise as the Fossil Host for 30 s, then victory)
XVPart IIIThe Turning YearPlayableGreenwood, Fae Court, World-TreeSeasons (the 20:00 clock is one year of four seasons, the World-Tree twice as fast), Bloom and Blight (grass dies where the army stands; the Wild heal on living ground), Thickets (Rot, Wither and fire burn them).Spring Returns (everything grows back); on the World-Tree the First Spring (with the Green Mother beaten, the planted dead rise and the run ends in victory)

The acts run in the final order (StageRegistry.ACT_ORDER, three Parts of five acts): Part I: the living (acts I to V); Part II: gods, hell and heaven (acts VI to X); Part III: beyond and before (acts XI to XV). Every act number, chapter, unlock and Soul Ash multiplier derives from that one list.

Every stage is a 20:00 countdown. The boss arrives at 17:00 (BOSS_TIME 1020 s). At 0:00 the Reckoning begins; dying after 0:00 is a victory. Soul Ash multipliers follow the per-act rule x1, x1.25, x1.5 (stage 1, 2, 3 of each act). Each stage opens when the previous stage's boss falls (the chain runs through all 45 in the order above).

The Last Line also promotes its Supers to zone minibosses at runtime (Liberty Heights: Blitz 17:30, Aurora 13:30, Atlas 8:30, Nightjar from 5:00). The Supers are listed with the Last Line enemies. Crimson March and the Graveyard have no flagged miniboss rows. Some minibosses are boss-fight pieces of the act's own rules (the Cherub of the Gate, the Herald of the Seventh Trumpet, the Gardener of Roots, Fenrir beside Odin).

The Reckoning Inquisitor ("Inquisitor of the End") is the Act I Reckoning kind and is counted in neither group.

Spells and evolutions (54 + 54)

12 base-game spells (3 starter spells and 9 later ones) and 42 act spells (three for each of the 14 later acts, each unlocked by a stage boss). Spell origins name the stage the spell was built for, with its act in the final order. Each has one evolution, delivered by a treasure chest once the spell and its paired passive are at Lv 5 and 8:00 has elapsed. Six active slots compete among spells and summon classes.

Synergies (14)

SynergyEffect
Shieldwall of the Damned
Warders raise bone barriers on your frontline warriors.
Volley of the Fallen
Mage explosions mark foes; archers deal bonus damage to marked foes.
March of the Deathless
Your summons move faster and slowly regenerate.
The Unholy Host
An unholy aura: all summons attack faster and take less damage.
Flesh Rampart
Abomination stomps stagger foes; warriors hit staggered foes harder.
Killing Field
Catapults aim at the foes an Abomination staggers and hit them harder.
Death from Above
Rogues hit swooped foes harder; the first hit on one resets the dash.
The Wild Hunt
A foe a Gargoyle swoops on becomes the pack's prey; bites on it hit harder.
Cold Blood
Rogues dash at chilled and frozen foes and hit them harder.
Shatterfall
Catapults aim at frozen foes; boulders hit frozen foes much harder.
Requiem
Mage explosions hit weakened foes harder and stretch the Dirge.
Baying of the Damned
Every Dirge sends the bone hounds into a frenzy.
The Charnel Menagerie
Four of the newer horrors: they deal more damage and return faster.
Bone Bastion
Summons near a Bone Golem take less damage, far less while it is planted.

Synergies switch on at Lv 2 of each required class. Bone Bastion (Bone Golem plus a Warrior or Abomination) was added with content wave 2; the Charnel Menagerie needs any 4 of the 7 newer classes. Only the classes named in the synergy rows take part: the act classes (from the Fallen Seraph through the Bound Oni to the Bound Ophan, Bonehorn and Ossuary Oak) have no dedicated synergies in the data.

Run systems, difficulty and modes

Difficulty levels

LevelBoss HPSoul AshDescription
Initiatex0.8x0.8Easier scaling. The Covenant grows stronger more slowly and hits softer.
Necromancerx1.0x1.0Standard. The Covenant as it was meant to be fought.
Lichx1.15x1.5Increased HP and aggression. Tougher soldiers close in faster.
Deathlordx1.3x2.0The hardest. Stronger, faster soldiers, and elites march among them.

Run modifiers

ModifierEffectSoul Ash bonus
Endless Crusade+30% enemy spawn rate (and a 30% larger horde on the field).+20%
Hardened Faith+25% enemy health (the boss gets a fifth of it).+20%
Divine Fury+20% enemy damage.+20%
Purge the UnholyMore Purifiers: x2.5 of them, and they join the march from 3:00.+15%
ScarcityGrave Feast drops are 60% rarer and heal half as much.+10%
Frail MasterThe necromancer starts with 30% less max HP.+15%
Vengeful DeadYour undead deal 20% more damage but have 30% less HP.+10%
Holy RetributionSlain elites burst into a ring of 8 radiant bolts.+15%

Profane Pact, Profane Oath and Hyper mode

  • Profane Pact: an in-run passive, 5 levels (to +25% spawn, +25% HP, +15% damage for +40% XP, +60% Soul Ash, +75% drop chance).
  • Profane Oath: an Ossuary option, 5 tiers of opt-in difficulty for richer rewards.
  • Hyper mode: unlocked by slaying Seraphine once. Growth part of enemy HP/damage scaling x2, stage boss HP x1.5, Soul Ash +100%. Hyper clears earn a gold badge per stage and character.

Ultimates

UltimateTaglineEffect
Dread Rally
Raise and rally the armyRaises every fallen summon, heals the army 30%, +40% damage and attack speed for 8 s, knocks foes back.
Sovereign's Decree
Your dead take the blowsFor 8 s every summon taunts foes near it and takes 50% less damage; you cannot be targeted.
Eclipse
Darkness stops the worldDarkness for 4 s: every foe on screen freezes (bosses are slowed 60%), then takes +30% damage for 6 s.
Grave Tide
The slain rise for youFor 10 s every foe that dies rises as a Risen fighting for you for 12 s.

Dread Rally is the default; the other three are earned by achievements. Grave Step is the dash (Shift / RB).

Power-ups

Six pickups: Magnet, Feast, Hyper, Stasis, Frenzy, Nova.

Game modes

  • Solo run (any unlocked stage, character, difficulty, modifiers, Hyper).
  • Online co-op: 2 players, lobby codes through a Cloudflare relay, one lockstep simulation, shared XP bar, downed and revived by the partner, enemies x2 spawns, boss HP x1.7. Same platform only.
  • Autotest and --coop-bot headless modes for development.

Platforms

  • Windows and Linux desktop builds.
  • Web build for desktop browsers (GitHub Pages).
  • Phones and tablets in landscape in the browser (touch controls, mobile UI scale, Reduced effects default).
  • Native Android and iOS apps: deferred, not built.
The Ossuary (meta-progression)

32 upgrades with 172 purchasable levels. 13 upgrades have levels 6-10, gated by difficulty clears (levels 6-7 Lich, 8-9 Deathlord, 10 Deathlord + Hyper). Soul Ash is kept on death and restarts its multiplier per act.

What the data does not say
  • Boss base HP is not shown: several data files hold per-phase or per-body values (Shogun, Vhal'Neth, Carmilla and the Elder), so a single number would mislead.
  • Hades' final phase name and Lilith's phase names are not itemised in the data headers.
  • The Act I run loop has no title in the data.
  • No full-clear playtime is stored in the data; the only figure is the 20:00 clock times the stage count.
  • Sound recipe counts are rows at the top level of each sound table and may include recipe variants.
  • Enemy rows include spawned sub-kinds (Lesser and Least Mass, Swarm Rocket, Decoy Drone, Shadow of Kage, Fossil Host and Last Claim helpers where they are rows) and boss-fight structures (Cerberus heads, Vhal'Neth arms, Leg Plates, Canopic Jars, barrows).
  • Origins of spells, passives, classes and characters come from the section comments in the data files; the act number in a comment is the one the row was built under, so the inventory rebuilds each origin from the stage's final act. The Fallen Seraph is shown under the Sanctum (unlocked by Seraphine).
  • Phase lists are hand-summarised from each boss data file's header; the files give HP shares and timers, not short names for every phase.
  • Hand-written text (phase lists, each act's shared rules and Reckoning, the planned section) is not read from data and must be updated when an act changes.
